Floral Park is a middle class neighborhood in the New York City borough of Queens. It is adjacent to the Village of Floral Park, which is in Nassau County. It may be distinguished from the latter by the use of the designation "North Floral Park" with a ZIP code of 11004.
Description
The neighborhood is part of Queens Community Board 13. Floral Park is a middle-class neighborhood that consists mostly of Cape Cod-style houses. Most of the houses were built after World War II to accommodate returning soldiers. Veterans today make up 11 percent of all residents in Floral Park, versus 6 percent citywide.
Union Turnpike is the border between the neighborhood of Glen Oaks to the north. The other boundaries of Floral Park are roughly Little Neck Parkway (252nd Street) to the west, Langdale Street to the east, and a diagonal boundary from Hillside Avenue at 271st Street to Jericho Turnpike at 257th Street to the south. The Nassau County village of the same name serves as the neighborhood's southern border, while North New Hyde Park lies east of the neighborhood. Floral Park is in close proximity to the Cross Island Parkway and the Grand Central Parkway.
Transportation
MTA New York City Transit buses serve Floral Park on the  local routes. They also operate the  express route to Midtown. In addition, MTA Bus Company operates the  express buses to Midtown. The neighborhood is also served by Nassau Inter-County Express on the .
Floral Park station – located in the adjacent, eponymous Nassau County village – is the closest service to the neighborhood on the Long Island Rail Road, which connects to both Penn Station and Grand Central Madison in Midtown Manhattan.
Notable people
Notable former and current residents include Robert Mapplethorpe, a photographer, who was born and raised in Floral Park, Queens, where members of his family attended Our Lady of the Snows Catholic School.
